transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-01-11 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam Patel - Redwood; Sofia Ramirez, Mark Ellis, Priya Nair - Aurora Finance

Summary: Quick Optimize walkthrough focusing on batching and prefix / KV cache recommendations. Demonstrated cost model examples showing token savings and latency tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: send security docs + pricing, run pilot benchmark with sample traces.

Topics: intro, current infra, traffic profile, latency SLO, batching primer, prefix vs KV caching, cost model walk-through, pilot scope, next steps

00:00 Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, um we'll do a quick agenda - me for context + pricing, Liam will do the deep dive on batching and KV cache, then Q&A
00:18 Sofia (Aurora): thanks Maya, quick context - we run customer support summarization and fraud detection pipelines; avg request payload ~600 tokens, multimodal in future but for now text, target p95 latency < 300ms for chat flows, cost is big driver
00:34 Liam (Redwood): great, and just to confirm are you currently on-prem or cloud? I remember you mentioned mixed cloud, right?
00:41 Mark (Aurora): yeah hybrid - most traffic in GCP, some legacy on-prem for PCI stuff; we can't send PII offsite without keys, so VPC or private deployment considerations apply
00:55 Liam: got it - we'll call out private/deploy options plus KMS integration. ok starting the walkthrough - first principle: batching reduces per-token compute overhead but increases queuing latency; for tail-sensitive chat flows small batch sizes often win, for high-throughput async jobs larger batches are better
01:20 Maya: and the KV/prefix cache is where we save tokens - if you have repeated prefixes (session history, user metadata) we can cache key/value activations so you don't resend the full history on every request
01:36 Priya (Aurora): is KV cache safe for PII? our security team will want to know retention and KMS controls
01:44 Maya: short answer yes - cache entries can be encrypted with customer KMS and TTLs enforced; we'll add the SOC2/network diagram in the pack
01:55 Liam: demo slide - here's a synthetic trace: 10k requests/day, avg tokens/request 600, typical session history 200 tokens repeated across 3 turns. With no cache baseline cost X. With prefix/KV cache we see ~50-65% token reduction on subsequent turns depending on how stable the prefix is
02:20 Sofia: wait 50-65%? can you show numbers?
02:26 Liam: sure - example: baseline cost per million tokens $15 (hosted API example), at 600 tokens * 10k reqs = 6M tokens/day, baseline daily cost ~ $90. If 60% of tokens are cached via KV, effective tokens billed drop to 2.4M -> ~$36/day. So roughly 60% cost reduction for that workload, caveats apply
02:56 Mark: these numbers assume same model and no quantization?
03:01 Liam: right, this is model-agnostic for the cache effect but runtime choices (quantization, model family) shift compute cost. We'll include alternate rows in the cost model spreadsheet for quantized vs full fp16 execution
03:15 Sofia: what's the latency hit for cache lookups? we can't accept >20ms extra on the hot path
03:22 Liam: typical KV lookup is ~1-5ms if colocated; in our hosted offering it's sub-10ms for hot cache. For private/dedicated you get even lower depending on topology. The bigger latency risk is batching queuing time, not cache lookup
03:40 Liam: demo: batching tradeoffs - continuous batching engine groups requests up to a max batch size or max wait time. For chat SLO 200-300ms we recommend max batch wait ~15-30ms and max batch size 8-16 depending on hardware and model. That preserves p95 while still giving some batching efficiency
04:05 Priya: can we control that per-route? some routes are high-sensitivity (auth) others are bulk async
04:12 Maya: yes per-route policies in Console - you can set batch windows, priority routing, fallback models. We'll show the Console in a minute
04:20 Liam: switching to the Console screenshot - route config, KV cache TTLs, and cost preview. Note: prefix cache vs full KV difference - prefix cache caches input token prefix embeddings at request time; KV cache stores decoder key/value states for autoregressive models to avoid recomputing earlier tokens
04:45 Sofia: ok prefix vs KV both help but KV cache seems more powerful for multi-turn chat?
04:52 Liam: correct - KV has more savings for long contexts because you avoid recomputing attention for the prefix; prefix caching is lighter-weight and sometimes easier to reason about for structured prompts
05:05 Mark: any infra changes to support KV? like memory overheads?
05:10 Liam: yes memory on the serving nodes goes up because KV stores activations; typical overheads: roughly 0.5-1.5x memory per live session depending on sequence length and quantization. But we provide eviction policies and TTLs so it scales predictably. We'll surface memory vs savings tradeoff in the spreadsheet
05:35 Sofia: how do you estimate cost delta for us specifically? we'll need p95/p99 targets and their throughput distribution
05:42 Liam: best is you send sample trace - we run a 5k-request benchmark that replays your traffic against candidate configs (hosted vs dedicated, quantization, batch windows, cache TTLs). We produce a table: latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens billed, and estimated monthly cost.
06:00 Maya: I'll attach the benchmark template + sample config. we'll also include an example pilot scope: 2-week pilot on dedicated pool or hosted reserved with traffic mirroring
06:10 Priya: about security - will logs contain user text? audit logs?
06:15 Maya: audit logs can be configured to redact PII, and we support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. For Private deployments you keep data on-prem. We'll include the security pack
06:25 Sofia: any competitors we should worry about? our procurement asked about Anthropic and OpenAI offerings
06:30 Maya: we compared in the deck - Anthropic has tight safety features, OpenAI has broad scale; our differentiation is cost-control knobs, per-route batching/cache controls, and rollout/observability to detect regressions in quality during model swaps
06:50 Liam: demo continued - cost model sheet shows scenarios: no cache, prefix cache (30% token reduction), KV cache (60% token reduction), plus rows for batch sizes 1/8/16. Example improvement: p95 latency change: batch 1 -> p95 220ms, batch 8 -> p95 260ms on same hw; but cost per token drops ~30%
07:20 Mark: do you autoscale dedicated pools when cache load increases?
07:26 Liam: autoscale is independent of cache; cache is per-instance; autoscale events spin up nodes with cold caches so initial miss rates spike but steady state benefits remain. We have warmup policies and prefetching strategies to reduce cold-start misses
07:45 Sofia: curious about cache consistency for user updates - if user state changes mid-session do we need to evict entries?
07:51 Liam: yes you can key cache entries by session+version and evict on write; TTLs help. For strong consistency you might prefer shorter TTLs or explicit invalidation via API
08:10 Maya: ok walking through a concrete pilot proposal: 2 weeks, we mirror 5k/day of traffic, run hosted reserved pool, enable KV cache with TTL 10 minutes, batching window 25ms, target p95 < 300ms. deliverable: benchmark report + cost delta + recommended config
08:35 Priya: procurement will need pricing for 3 scenarios: hosted pay-as-you-go, hosted reserved 6mo, private deployment estimate
08:45 Maya: we'll include those three and call out one-time onboarding and SSO/KMS integration fees in the quote
08:55 Sofia: any gotchas we should be aware of?
09:00 Liam: watch out for adversarial prompts that bust caching (lots of unique prefixes) - in those cases caching gives less benefit. Also be careful with batching for low-volume interactive routes; batching can actually increase p95 if misconfigured
09:18 Mark: can we do A/B test to compare results quality when using prefix cache vs full resend? we worry about regression in model output
09:25 Liam: yes - Console supports rollout A/B, and we can run evals on your prompt set. we'll tie regressions to alerts in Optimize so you get notified if quality drops after enabling cache or changing batch policy
09:40 Sofia: ok great - can you also share a short runbook for how to set TTLs and eviction in practice?
09:45 Maya: yes we'll include a 'cache tuning playbook' with heuristics: prefer KV for multi-turn, start TTL at 5-15m for support flows, evict on critical user updates, and increase batch window gradually while monitoring p95
10:05 Liam: quick Q from my side - do you have a target cost per 1M requests we should aim for?
10:12 Sofia: procurement target is to get total LLM cost under $10k/mo for the pilot workload, otherwise they'll push for vendor consolidation
10:20 Liam: okay that's helpful - we'll tune the pilot to aim under that with aggressive KV caching + quantized model where feasible
10:30 Maya: wrapping up, agreed next steps and owners as we'll put in CRM
10:38 Sofia: thanks team, we'll send the logs and calendar for follow-up
10:42 Priya: thanks, bye

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions like "K-V cash" or "Redwood Opti maze" because of auto-caption errors. There were intermittent crosstalks during the demo slide load - timestamps approximate.

End of call.
